userRequest: You are an agent version tracker. Check for new releases of the ORIGINAL upstream agent CLI products -- NOT our babysitter plugin packages. Build atlas with npm run build --workspace=@a5c-ai/atlas. Get the target list using the same logic as scripts/sync-external-plugin-repos.mjs buildTargetsFromCatalog by importing packages/atlas/dist/catalog/sdk.js and filtering listPluginTargetDescriptors() for externalRepo. Also check adapter source for additional npm install -g commands using grep -r 'npm install -g' packages/adapters/codecs/src/ | grep -v node_modules | grep -v test. Merge both lists. Exclude all @a5c-ai/* packages. For each upstream agent, check latest published version: npm view <package>@latest version for npm packages, web search for agents distributed differently. Compare against AgentVersion records in packages/atlas/graph/agent-stack/agent-versions/ and products in packages/atlas/graph/agent-stack/products/. For new versions not in the graph, search for release notes/changelog/blog posts, create or update AgentVersion YAML, and note capability changes, new CLI flags, breaking changes, transport/API changes. If graph files changed, rebuild Atlas, create branch agent-versions/daily-$(date +%Y-%m-%d), commit all changes, create one PR against staging. For each new agent+version pair, check gh issue list --label agent-version-update --search '<agent> <version>'; if none exists, create an issue labeled agent-version-update,graph-update. Issue bodies must contain actual research, exact old/new versions, real release links, specific change summaries, likely affected system surfaces, install method/package changes, migration steps, and a change-specific assimilation checklist. Print a summary table with all agents checked. Cover every upstream agent systematically.
